newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian light crudes find limited buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Asian light crudes find limited buying interest.

text.p: Asia's light sweet crude market weakened as ample supplies were finding very limited buying interest from refiners.
A July cargo of Cossack was traded between majors late last week at a substantial discount of $1.10 per barrel under the Tapis APPI, double the normal discount for Cossack trades.
A western trader was also widely heard holding prompt June Australian Harriet and Barrow Island which it was trying to sell into Indonesia.
With allocations of July Belida higher due to the turnaround at Balikpapan, sentiment on the market was bearish.

But the heavy sweet crude market was stronger, on expectations of increased utility demand from Japan in July. Japan's Federation of Electric Power Cos said earlier said there could be record power demand this summer, even on normal temperatures.
Traders said Japanese utility demand for direct burning Widuri in July were expected to double from normal requirements to around 900,000 barrels, traders said.
Most shosha have already committed their cargoes into Japan, leaving two shosha and the Widuri equity producer holding July barrels, which they offered above ICP +20.
In the Middle East crude market, an overhang in July supplies kept levels depressed. Three cargoes of Lower Zakum and one and a half cargoes of Murban were still available for July.
With most refiners already covered, traders expected these cargoes to find homes once August trading starts and that a repeat of the early July market would occur.
In July, availabilities of end June supplies dragged down the prices of early July trades.
But sellers pointed out that in July, there were at least seven cargoes of end June material still on offer, a much bigger volume than currently available for July.
